a: WCAG is the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (A, AA, AAA levels).
POUR: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust — WCAG principles.
Text needs sufficient contrast against backgrounds (WCAG ratios).
Screen readers announce page content using semantics and ARIA.
Skip links let keyboard users jump to main content.
Label every input, associate errors, and do not rely on color alone.
Buttons/links need accessible names via text or aria-label.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion for users sensitive to animation.
Avoid focus traps that prevent Tab from leaving a component.
ARIA roles describe UI widgets when native HTML semantics are insufficient.
